name: story_beat_templates
description: Named beat-sheet templates for fiction and narrative: screenwriting sheets, mythic journeys, classical and world dramaturgy, genre structures, and episodic or framed forms. Every record carries 'beats': [{name, position 0-1, purpose}], with 'acts' and a valence 'curve' where the tradition defines one.

screenwriting_sheets.name: save the cat beat sheet
screenwriting_sheets.definition: Blake Snyder's fifteen-beat commercial screenplay template, pinned to fixed page positions and driven by a thematic lesson the hero refuses until the last act.

beats.name: opening image
beats.purpose: show the hero's world in one image that the ending will answer

beats.name: theme stated
beats.purpose: let a minor character say the lesson the hero cannot yet hear

beats.name: setup
beats.purpose: establish the ordinary life, the supporting cast, and the thing that is missing

beats.name: catalyst
beats.purpose: break the status quo with an event that cannot be undone

beats.name: debate
beats.purpose: let the hero resist, weigh the cost, and voice the question the act will answer

beats.name: break into two
beats.purpose: have the hero choose the new world rather than be dragged into it

beats.name: b story
beats.purpose: open the relationship line that will carry the theme

beats.name: fun and games
beats.purpose: deliver the premise the audience came for, at low cost to the hero

beats.name: midpoint
beats.purpose: raise the stakes with a false victory or false defeat that makes the goal public

beats.name: bad guys close in
beats.purpose: tighten external pressure while the hero's own team fractures

beats.name: all is lost
beats.purpose: strip the hero of the thing the midpoint promised; something dies

beats.name: dark night of the soul
beats.purpose: hold the hero in the loss long enough for the theme to land

beats.name: break into three
beats.purpose: fuse the a and b stories into a plan the hero could not have made before

beats.name: finale
beats.purpose: prove the change by action, dismantling the opposition top down

beats.name: final image
beats.purpose: mirror the opening image so the distance travelled is visible

screenwriting_sheets.aka: Snyder beat sheet, the fifteen beats
screenwriting_sheets.register: commercial screenplay and plot-forward genre fiction; the default vocabulary of American development notes
screenwriting_sheets.caution: The page positions are habits of a 110-page feature, not laws; hit them in a novel and every book comes out the same length in the same places.

screenwriting_sheets.name: syd field paradigm
screenwriting_sheets.definition: The three-act paradigm built on two plot points and two pinches, with act two exactly twice the length of the acts around it.

beats.name: opening image
beats.purpose: set tone and premise in the first minute of screen time

beats.name: setup
beats.purpose: give the audience who, where, and what is at stake before anything moves

beats.name: inciting incident
beats.purpose: involve the protagonist emotionally in a problem not of their choosing

beats.name: plot point one
beats.purpose: spin the story into a new direction and lock act two shut behind it

beats.name: first pinch
beats.purpose: remind the audience of the antagonistic force with a direct squeeze

beats.name: midpoint
beats.purpose: split act two with an event that changes what the protagonist is doing and why

beats.name: second pinch
beats.purpose: return the pressure at greater cost, now aimed at what the hero values

beats.name: plot point two
beats.purpose: reverse the situation and set the single question act three will answer

beats.name: climax
beats.purpose: answer the dramatic question in action, not explanation

beats.name: resolution
beats.purpose: settle the new status quo and get out

screenwriting_sheets.aka: the paradigm, three-act with plot points
screenwriting_sheets.register: feature screenplay; the baseline against which most other sheets define themselves
screenwriting_sheets.caution: It describes where turns land, not what happens between them; a paradigm outline with an empty act two is the classic failure.

screenwriting_sheets.name: eight-sequence approach
screenwriting_sheets.definition: A feature told as eight roughly equal sequences, each with its own goal, obstacle and small climax, inherited from the reel lengths of early cinema.

beats.name: sequence one: status quo and disturbance
beats.purpose: establish the world and break it before the audience settles

beats.name: sequence two: the new dramatic question
beats.purpose: let the attempt to restore normality fail and pose the real question

beats.name: sequence three: first attempts
beats.purpose: commit to a plan in the new world and learn its rules the hard way

beats.name: sequence four: complications mount
beats.purpose: exhaust the obvious solutions on the way to the midpoint

beats.name: sequence five: reversal and new direction
beats.purpose: turn the story on a revelation that resets the objective

beats.name: sequence six: opposition at full strength
beats.purpose: bring the antagonist's best move against a depleted hero

beats.name: sequence seven: last twists before the end
beats.purpose: show the apparent solution failing and force the final choice

beats.name: sequence eight: resolution
beats.purpose: settle the dramatic question and close the sequence chain

screenwriting_sheets.register: feature film and long-form television; useful for novelists who think in chapters
screenwriting_sheets.caution: Each sequence needs its own tension, not a slice of the main one, or the film becomes eight scenes of throat-clearing.

screenwriting_sheets.name: story circle
screenwriting_sheets.definition: Dan Harmon's eight-step circle: a character in comfort wants something, crosses into an unfamiliar world, adapts, gets what they wanted, pays for it, and returns changed.

beats.name: in comfort
beats.purpose: place the character in a zone of routine and competence

beats.name: want
beats.purpose: surface the lack that routine cannot satisfy

beats.name: cross into the unfamiliar
beats.purpose: put the character somewhere the old rules do not apply

beats.name: adapt
beats.purpose: make them pay a learning cost, then improvise

beats.name: find
beats.purpose: give them the thing they wanted, in a form they did not expect

beats.name: pay the price
beats.purpose: charge them for it; the want and the need part ways here

beats.name: return
beats.purpose: carry them back across the threshold, pursued or diminished

beats.name: changed
beats.purpose: show the old world through new capacity

screenwriting_sheets.register: half-hour television, episodic serials, short fiction; scales down better than most feature sheets
screenwriting_sheets.caution: The circle is per character, not per episode; running it once for the ensemble flattens everyone into the same lesson.

screenwriting_sheets.name: seven-point structure
screenwriting_sheets.definition: A structure planned backwards from resolution to hook, using two plot turns and two pinch points to force a state that is the opposite of where the character began.

beats.name: hook
beats.purpose: open in the state that the resolution will invert

beats.name: first plot turn
beats.purpose: introduce the change that makes the story necessary

beats.name: first pinch
beats.purpose: apply antagonist pressure and show what losing would mean

beats.name: midpoint
beats.purpose: flip the character from reacting to acting

beats.name: second pinch
beats.purpose: take away the support the plan depended on

beats.name: second plot turn
beats.purpose: hand over the last missing piece needed to win

beats.name: resolution
beats.purpose: arrive at the endpoint the hook was written against

screenwriting_sheets.register: genre novels, especially fantasy and thriller; a planning tool more than a drafting one
screenwriting_sheets.caution: Because it is designed end-first, a weak resolution poisons every earlier beat.

screenwriting_sheets.name: nutshell technique
screenwriting_sheets.definition: Jill Chamberlain's eight-element frame in which a protagonist's flaw and want collide at a point of no return, producing a catch that only a climactic choice can resolve.

beats.name: setup want
beats.purpose: name the thing the protagonist thinks will fix their life

beats.name: flaw
beats.purpose: expose the controllable fault that makes the want the wrong cure

beats.name: point of no return
beats.purpose: commit them to a course they cannot walk back

beats.name: the catch
beats.purpose: attach an unwanted condition to the thing they are getting

beats.name: crisis
beats.purpose: strand them in the exact situation the flaw guaranteed

beats.name: climactic choice
beats.purpose: force a choice between the want and the truth

beats.name: final step
beats.purpose: act once more against the flaw, in public

beats.name: strength
beats.purpose: leave them holding the virtue that the flaw was hiding

screenwriting_sheets.register: screenplay diagnosis; a fast test for whether a premise is a story or a situation
screenwriting_sheets.caution: It is a coherence check, not a page plan — nothing in it tells you what fills the middle hour.

screenwriting_sheets.name: six-stage plot structure
screenwriting_sheets.definition: Michael Hauge's six stages of the outer journey, separated by five turning points, tracked against a hero's movement from identity to essence.

beats.name: setup
beats.purpose: show the everyday life and the mask the hero lives behind

beats.name: turning point: opportunity
beats.purpose: offer a new situation that creates a desire

beats.name: new situation
beats.purpose: let the hero explore the new world and glimpse what life could be

beats.name: turning point: change of plans
beats.purpose: convert vague desire into a specific visible goal

beats.name: progress
beats.purpose: let the plan work well enough to raise the hero's investment

beats.name: turning point: point of no return
beats.purpose: burn the retreat; commitment becomes total

beats.name: complications and higher stakes
beats.purpose: make every obstacle cost more than the last

beats.name: turning point: major setback
beats.purpose: take away the goal and the mask together

beats.name: final push
beats.purpose: have the hero act from essence instead of identity

beats.name: turning point: climax
beats.purpose: settle the outer goal and the inner cost in one confrontation

beats.name: aftermath
beats.purpose: show the life that is possible now that the mask is gone

screenwriting_sheets.register: screenplay and commercial fiction; strongest where inner and outer journeys must be visibly braided
screenwriting_sheets.caution: The inner-journey vocabulary tempts writers to state the change in dialogue; the structure requires it be shown at each turning point.

screenwriting_sheets.name: twenty-two-step anatomy
screenwriting_sheets.definition: John Truby's organic sequence, in which a haunted hero's need, desire and moral weakness drive revelations, plans and counterattacks toward a self-revelation earned in battle.

beats.name: weakness and need
beats.purpose: give the hero a psychological and a moral flaw before anything happens

beats.name: ghost and story world
beats.purpose: plant the past wound and the world it made

beats.name: inciting event
beats.purpose: disturb the world in a way that demands a response

beats.name: desire
beats.purpose: state the concrete goal that will carry the plot

beats.name: ally
beats.purpose: give the hero someone to argue the theme with

beats.name: opponent and mystery
beats.purpose: introduce the rival who wants the same thing and hides information

beats.name: fake-ally opponent
beats.purpose: place a friendly face on the opposition

beats.name: first revelation and decision
beats.purpose: change the hero's plan with new information

beats.name: plan
beats.purpose: let the hero name the strategy that gives the middle its shape

beats.name: opponent's counterattack
beats.purpose: show the antagonist acting on their own superior plan

beats.name: drive
beats.purpose: run the escalating attempts, each with a moral cost

beats.name: attack by ally
beats.purpose: have the person who loves the hero name what they are becoming

beats.name: apparent defeat
beats.purpose: take the desire away and expose the need

beats.name: second revelation and obsessive drive
beats.purpose: restart the pursuit with new information and less restraint

beats.name: audience revelation
beats.purpose: let the audience learn what the hero does not, and wait

beats.name: third revelation and decision
beats.purpose: give the hero the fact the audience already holds

beats.name: gate, gauntlet, visit to death
beats.purpose: compress the pressure and make mortality explicit

beats.name: battle
beats.purpose: settle the conflict of values in physical or verbal combat

beats.name: self-revelation
beats.purpose: make the hero see the moral truth about themselves

beats.name: moral decision
beats.purpose: prove the revelation by an act with a price

beats.name: new equilibrium
beats.purpose: leave the world permanently altered by the change

screenwriting_sheets.aka: Truby's twenty-two steps, the anatomy of story
screenwriting_sheets.register: literary-leaning screenplay and novel; the most morally explicit of the commercial sheets
screenwriting_sheets.caution: Twenty-two obligatory steps in ninety minutes will feel like a checklist; treat weakness, revelation and self-revelation as load-bearing and the rest as optional.

screenwriting_sheets.name: story spine
screenwriting_sheets.definition: Kenn Adams' improv sentence frame — once upon a time, every day, until one day, because of that, until finally, and ever since then — which yields causal rather than episodic plotting.

beats.name: once upon a time
beats.purpose: name the character and the world in one line

beats.name: every day
beats.purpose: establish the routine that the story will break

beats.name: until one day
beats.purpose: introduce the single disturbance everything else follows from

beats.name: because of that
beats.purpose: chain the first consequence, not the next event

beats.name: because of that
beats.purpose: escalate the consequence chain toward a corner

beats.name: because of that
beats.purpose: exhaust the options the chain has left

beats.name: until finally
beats.purpose: resolve the disturbance in the only remaining way

beats.name: and ever since then
beats.purpose: state the new normal, which is also the theme

screenwriting_sheets.aka: Pixar story spine, the improv spine
screenwriting_sheets.register: pitching, children's stories, early premise testing; the fastest structural check there is
screenwriting_sheets.caution: "And then" instead of "because of that" is the tell that a plot is episodic; the spine exists to catch exactly that.

screenwriting_sheets.name: eight-point arc
screenwriting_sheets.definition: Nigel Watts' compact arc — stasis, trigger, quest, surprise, critical choice, climax, reversal, resolution — in which the choice, not the fight, is the moral centre.

beats.name: stasis
beats.purpose: show the ordinary state the trigger will break

beats.name: trigger
beats.purpose: let something outside the character's control start the story

beats.name: quest
beats.purpose: send the character after the thing the trigger made necessary

beats.name: surprise
beats.purpose: run the obstacles and reversals that make the middle

beats.name: critical choice
beats.purpose: force a deliberate decision that reveals character

beats.name: climax
beats.purpose: deliver the highest-consequence result of that choice

beats.name: reversal
beats.purpose: change the character's status or self-understanding for good

beats.name: resolution
beats.purpose: return to a stasis that is not the one we started in

screenwriting_sheets.register: literary short story and novel; a gentle alternative to page-pinned screenwriting sheets
screenwriting_sheets.caution: Surprise is one beat here but half the book in practice; do not let its single line license a slack middle.

screenwriting_sheets.name: four-part story structure
screenwriting_sheets.definition: Larry Brooks' four contexts — orphan, wanderer, warrior, martyr — separated by the first plot point, midpoint context shift and second plot point, with pinch points at the quarter marks.

beats.name: hook
beats.purpose: buy the reader's attention in the opening pages

beats.name: setup: the orphan
beats.purpose: show a protagonist without agency in the coming conflict

beats.name: inciting incident
beats.purpose: put the antagonistic force on the board

beats.name: first plot point
beats.purpose: define the need, the stakes and the opposition in one turn

beats.name: response: the wanderer
beats.purpose: let the protagonist react, flee and fail to understand

beats.name: first pinch point
beats.purpose: show the antagonist's power without the protagonist's mediation

beats.name: midpoint context shift
beats.purpose: give the protagonist information that turns reaction into attack

beats.name: attack: the warrior
beats.purpose: run proactive attempts that fail for better reasons

beats.name: second pinch point
beats.purpose: reassert the threat at its most direct

beats.name: second plot point
beats.purpose: deliver the last new information the ending will use

beats.name: resolution: the martyr
beats.purpose: let the protagonist act as the sole agent of the solution

beats.name: climax
beats.purpose: settle the conflict with no rescue from outside

beats.name: denouement
beats.purpose: show the changed world briefly and stop

screenwriting_sheets.aka: story engineering four parts, four-box structure
screenwriting_sheets.register: commercial novel planning; unusually explicit about what the protagonist may and may not do in each quarter
screenwriting_sheets.caution: The rule that the hero cannot be rescued is the point of the martyr quarter; break it and the whole scheme collapses into coincidence.

screenwriting_sheets.name: five commandments of storytelling
screenwriting_sheets.definition: The Story Grid unit — inciting incident, progressive complications, crisis, climax, resolution — applied fractally to scene, sequence, act and global story.

beats.name: inciting incident
beats.purpose: upset the life balance of the unit's protagonist

beats.name: progressive complications
beats.purpose: close off options until only bad ones remain

beats.name: crisis
beats.purpose: pose a best-bad or irreconcilable-goods dilemma

beats.name: climax
beats.purpose: answer the dilemma with a choice, not an accident

beats.name: resolution
beats.purpose: show the consequence and hand off to the next unit

screenwriting_sheets.aka: the five commandments, Story Grid unit
screenwriting_sheets.register: any length, any genre; the smallest complete structural unit in the commercial tradition
screenwriting_sheets.caution: A scene missing the crisis question is the commonest cause of flat middles — and the commandments are a diagnostic for it, not a page plan.

screenwriting_sheets.name: story-value progression
screenwriting_sheets.definition: Robert McKee's value-charged design, in which each scene turns a named value from positive to negative or back, and act climaxes turn it further than any scene inside them.

beats.name: opening value state
beats.purpose: establish where the governing value sits before the story moves

beats.name: inciting incident
beats.purpose: swing the value hard enough that balance must be restored

beats.name: object of desire
beats.purpose: let the protagonist name what would restore it

beats.name: first act climax
beats.purpose: turn the value further than any preceding scene

beats.name: progressive complications
beats.purpose: widen the gap between expectation and result, scene by scene

beats.name: midpoint reversal
beats.purpose: invert the value so the pursuit changes character

beats.name: deepening complications
beats.purpose: spend the remaining sources of conflict from outer to inner

beats.name: second act climax
beats.purpose: leave the protagonist with no conservative options

beats.name: crisis dilemma
beats.purpose: put the true self on the line in a single choice

beats.name: story climax
beats.purpose: turn the value absolutely and irreversibly

beats.name: resolution
beats.purpose: let the audience feel the new equilibrium settle

screenwriting_sheets.register: screenplay and literary fiction; the discipline that keeps scenes from being conversations
screenwriting_sheets.caution: If you cannot name the value a scene turns, the scene is exposition wearing a costume — but naming it aloud in dialogue is the cure that kills.

screenwriting_sheets.name: w-plot
screenwriting_sheets.definition: A double-dip shape: two descents into failure with a deceptive high point between them, so the midpoint peak reads as false confidence.

beats.name: opening stability
beats.purpose: start on level ground so the first fall registers

beats.name: trigger
beats.purpose: disturb the balance and set the pursuit

beats.name: first descent
beats.purpose: fail in a way the protagonist believes is recoverable

beats.name: recovery and new approach
beats.purpose: climb with a smarter plan and better allies

beats.name: false peak
beats.purpose: grant a revelation or victory that looks like the ending

beats.name: second descent begins
beats.purpose: turn the peak's cost into escalating loss

beats.name: lowest point
beats.purpose: reach a worse floor than the first, with fewer resources

beats.name: final climb
beats.purpose: rebuild from what survived the second fall

beats.name: transformed stability
beats.purpose: end higher than the opening, but not where the false peak promised

screenwriting_sheets.register: novels and long-form drama that need two full reversals rather than one
screenwriting_sheets.caution: The second fall must cost something the first did not, or the shape reads as repetition rather than escalation.

mythic_journeys.name: hero's journey
mythic_journeys.definition: Vogler's twelve-stage working of the monomyth: an ordinary hero is called across a threshold, tested, brought to an ordeal, and returned home carrying something the old world needs.

beats.name: ordinary world
beats.purpose: establish the life and the lack the adventure will address

beats.name: call to adventure
beats.purpose: deliver the summons that makes staying impossible

beats.name: refusal of the call
beats.purpose: voice the fear and the cost before the hero moves

beats.name: meeting the mentor
beats.purpose: supply courage, a lesson, or a tool the hero cannot yet use well

beats.name: crossing the threshold
beats.purpose: commit to the special world with its unfamiliar rules

beats.name: tests, allies, enemies
beats.purpose: teach hero and reader the new world through trial and company

beats.name: approach to the inmost cave
beats.purpose: plan, hesitate, and let the team's fractures show

beats.name: the ordeal
beats.purpose: bring the hero to a death — literal, symbolic, or of the old self

beats.name: reward
beats.purpose: seize what the ordeal was for, along with its complications

beats.name: the road back
beats.purpose: start home under pursuit; the special world does not release cleanly

beats.name: resurrection
beats.purpose: test the transformation at the highest stakes of the story

beats.name: return with the elixir
beats.purpose: bring back something that heals the ordinary world

mythic_journeys.aka: the monomyth, Vogler's twelve stages, the writer's journey
mythic_journeys.register: fantasy, adventure, coming-of-age, and any narrative whose subject is initiation
mythic_journeys.caution: It is a description of a pattern in myth, not a plotting requirement; forcing mentors and elixirs onto domestic or ensemble stories produces pastiche.

mythic_journeys.name: monomyth departure-initiation-return
mythic_journeys.definition: Campbell's three-movement scheme in its own terms, running from the call through the belly of the whale and the road of trials to the freedom to live.

beats.name: call to adventure
beats.purpose: open the world with a summons the hero did not seek

beats.name: refusal and supernatural aid
beats.purpose: refuse, then receive protection from an unexpected quarter

beats.name: crossing the first threshold
beats.purpose: pass the guardian that separates the known from the unknown

beats.name: belly of the whale
beats.purpose: swallow the hero whole; the old identity stops functioning

beats.name: road of trials
beats.purpose: run the sequence of ordeals that remakes capacity

beats.name: meeting with the goddess
beats.purpose: offer union with the source of life or love

beats.name: temptation and atonement
beats.purpose: face the seduction that would end the journey, then the holder of ultimate power

beats.name: apotheosis
beats.purpose: grant the expanded understanding the trials were for

beats.name: the ultimate boon
beats.purpose: obtain the object or knowledge the quest named

beats.name: refusal of the return
beats.purpose: let the hero prefer the transfigured world to the ordinary one

beats.name: magic flight and rescue
beats.purpose: escape with the boon, helped from outside if pursuit is winning

beats.name: crossing the return threshold
beats.purpose: re-enter the ordinary world and find it unchanged and unimpressed

beats.name: master of two worlds
beats.purpose: hold both realms at once without belonging only to either

mythic_journeys.register: myth, epic, folklore studies; the source text that the screenwriting versions compress
mythic_journeys.caution: Campbell was cataloguing comparative myth, not designing plots; the seventeen stages rarely appear complete in any single story, and no story needs them all.

mythic_journeys.name: heroine's journey
mythic_journeys.definition: Maureen Murdock's cycle of separation and reunion: a woman succeeds by the terms of a masculine order, finds the success hollow, descends, and integrates what she rejected.

beats.name: separation from the feminine
beats.purpose: reject the mother, the domestic, or the devalued inheritance

beats.name: identification with the masculine
beats.purpose: adopt the values and mentors of the dominant order

beats.name: road of trials
beats.purpose: defeat the ogres and myths that stand between her and achievement

beats.name: the illusory boon of success
beats.purpose: grant everything she set out to win

beats.name: awakening to aridity
beats.purpose: let the achievement register as empty and the body register the cost

beats.name: descent to the goddess
beats.purpose: strip the identity down in the underworld of grief and rage

beats.name: yearning to reconnect
beats.purpose: surface the longing for what was abandoned at the start

beats.name: healing the mother-daughter split
beats.purpose: reclaim the inheritance she refused

beats.name: healing the wounded masculine
beats.purpose: withdraw the projections placed on the men in her life

beats.name: integration
beats.purpose: hold both principles without discarding either

mythic_journeys.aka: Murdock's heroine's journey, the descent-and-integration cycle
mythic_journeys.register: literary and contemporary fiction, memoir; a psychological rather than adventure structure
mythic_journeys.caution: It is a shape about internal division, not gender essence; read as a checklist of feminine traits it becomes the cliché it was written against.

mythic_journeys.name: the virgin's promise
mythic_journeys.definition: Kim Hudson's thirteen-beat arc of creative awakening, in which a protagonist bound by a dependent world builds a secret life, is caught, and forces the kingdom to reorganize around her true self.

beats.name: dependent world
beats.purpose: show the world that defines her by its needs

beats.name: price of conformity
beats.purpose: make the cost of the mask visible and daily

beats.name: opportunity to shine
beats.purpose: offer a glimpse of the talent or desire she has suppressed

beats.name: dresses the part
beats.purpose: let her try the other life on in a small, deniable way

beats.name: secret world
beats.purpose: build a hidden space where the true self can practise

beats.name: no longer fits her world
beats.purpose: make the double life mechanically impossible to sustain

beats.name: caught shining
beats.purpose: expose the secret before she is ready to defend it

beats.name: gives up what kept her stuck
beats.purpose: surrender the belief or safety that bought her the old place

beats.name: kingdom in chaos
beats.purpose: let her refusal destabilize everyone who depended on it

beats.name: wanders in the wilderness
beats.purpose: leave her with neither the old world nor the secret one

beats.name: chooses her light
beats.purpose: make the choice for the authentic self with the cost fully known

beats.name: the re-ordering
beats.purpose: have the kingdom rearrange itself around who she now is

beats.name: the kingdom is brighter
beats.purpose: show the community better off for the upheaval

mythic_journeys.aka: the virgin arc, feminine creative-awakening arc
mythic_journeys.register: coming-of-age, romance, and any story where the antagonist is a role rather than a villain
mythic_journeys.caution: Its conflict is between a self and a community, not a hero and an enemy — imported villains flatten it into an ordinary quest.

mythic_journeys.name: voyage and return
mythic_journeys.definition: Booker's shape in which an ordinary protagonist falls into a strange world, is fascinated, then endangered, and escapes home with the world unchanged but themselves altered.

beats.name: the ordinary world
beats.purpose: establish an unremarkable life with a small restlessness

beats.name: the fall
beats.purpose: drop the protagonist into a place that runs on other rules

beats.name: initial fascination
beats.purpose: let the strangeness delight before it threatens

beats.name: growing unease
beats.purpose: turn the marvellous slightly wrong

beats.name: frustration
beats.purpose: trap the protagonist in the logic of the other world

beats.name: nightmare
beats.purpose: make the strange world actively lethal

beats.name: the escape
beats.purpose: break out by a thrilling margin

beats.name: return home
beats.purpose: restore the ordinary world exactly as it was

beats.name: changed by the journey
beats.purpose: show what the traveller understands that no one at home does

mythic_journeys.register: portal fantasy, satire, travel narrative, and dream stories
mythic_journeys.caution: The home world must stay unchanged for the shape to mean anything; fix it on the way out and the story becomes a quest instead.

mythic_journeys.name: overcoming the monster
mythic_journeys.definition: Booker's confrontation shape: a community is threatened by a devouring power, the hero prepares, is nearly consumed, finds the weakness, and kills it.

beats.name: the shadow falls
beats.purpose: establish the threat and the community it feeds on

beats.name: the call to confront
beats.purpose: assign the hero the task no one else will take

beats.name: preparation and allies
beats.purpose: gather weapons, knowledge, and companions

beats.name: the dream stage
beats.purpose: let early success suggest the monster is beatable

beats.name: frustration
beats.purpose: reveal the true scale of the thing

beats.name: the nightmare
beats.purpose: put the hero inside the monster's power, nearly consumed

beats.name: discovery of the weakness
beats.purpose: find the flaw that makes the impossible possible

beats.name: the killing stroke
beats.purpose: destroy the monster at the last possible moment

beats.name: restoration
beats.purpose: return the community to life and reward the hero

mythic_journeys.register: horror, thriller, action, and folk tale
mythic_journeys.caution: The monster must be genuinely stronger than the hero until the discovery, or the middle has no fear in it.

mythic_journeys.name: the quest plot
mythic_journeys.definition: Booker's journey toward a known distant goal: a company sets out from an intolerable situation, survives ordeals and temptations, and arrives to find the last obstacles the hardest.

beats.name: the oppressive situation
beats.purpose: make staying home unbearable and the goal necessary

beats.name: the call to journey
beats.purpose: name the destination and what waits there

beats.name: gathering companions
beats.purpose: assemble a company whose skills and frictions will both matter

beats.name: setting out
beats.purpose: run the first obstacles and establish the cost of travel

beats.name: temptations and tests
beats.purpose: offer easier lives that would end the quest

beats.name: arrival and frustration
beats.purpose: reach the destination and find the real difficulty begins there

beats.name: the final ordeals
beats.purpose: impose the guarded last trials, at the highest cost so far

beats.name: achieving the goal
beats.purpose: win the object or truth the journey named

beats.name: return and renewal
beats.purpose: carry the prize back and repair the situation that sent them

mythic_journeys.register: epic fantasy, adventure, road narrative, and pilgrimage
mythic_journeys.caution: Episodes on the road must change the company, not merely delay it, or the quest becomes a travelogue with a deadline.

mythic_journeys.name: rebirth plot
mythic_journeys.definition: Booker's shape of frozen life and thaw: a protagonist falls under a dark power, sinks into a living death, and is released by an act of love or recognition from outside.

beats.name: falling under shadow
beats.purpose: place the protagonist under a power they underestimate

beats.name: seeming stability
beats.purpose: let life proceed as if the shadow were survivable

beats.name: the dark power stirs
beats.purpose: close the trap and end the illusion of control

beats.name: deepening imprisonment
beats.purpose: narrow the world to the terms of the affliction

beats.name: the living death
beats.purpose: hold the protagonist in stasis long enough for it to feel permanent

beats.name: the redeeming figure
beats.purpose: bring a force of love or truth that does not accept the stasis

beats.name: the awakening
beats.purpose: crack the spell and restore agency

beats.name: the miraculous release
beats.purpose: break the dark power's hold decisively

beats.name: the new life
beats.purpose: show a life reorganized around what the thaw revealed

mythic_journeys.register: Christmas stories, fairy tale, literary transformation narratives
mythic_journeys.caution: Because the rescue comes from outside, the protagonist risks passivity; give the awakening an act they must perform themselves.

mythic_journeys.name: katabasis descent
mythic_journeys.definition: The underworld journey: a living protagonist crosses into the realm of the dead for knowledge, a person, or a debt, and returns under a condition that must not be broken.

beats.name: the unbearable loss
beats.purpose: establish what is missing that the living world cannot restore

beats.name: consulting the guide
beats.purpose: learn the route, the price, and the rule that governs return

beats.name: the crossing
beats.purpose: pay the ferryman and pass the boundary the living do not pass

beats.name: the shades
beats.purpose: meet the dead who explain what the protagonist could not see above

beats.name: the audience with the ruler
beats.purpose: petition the power that holds what was lost

beats.name: the condition
beats.purpose: receive the boon bound to a prohibition

beats.name: the ascent
beats.purpose: climb back with the condition pressing at every step

beats.name: the broken rule
beats.purpose: test the prohibition where the loss is felt most

beats.name: return to the living
beats.purpose: come back changed, carrying knowledge instead of the thing sought

mythic_journeys.register: myth, tragedy, literary fiction, and grief narratives; also a chapter shape inside longer works
mythic_journeys.caution: The condition is the story; a descent whose rule costs nothing to keep is only a tour.

mythic_journeys.name: wuxia jianghu journey
mythic_journeys.definition: The martial-hero arc: an orphaned talent trains under a master, rises in the jianghu, is betrayed into exile, achieves a breakthrough in isolation, and returns to settle the debt.

beats.name: humble origins
beats.purpose: place the hero low, orphaned, or dishonoured

beats.name: discovery of talent
beats.purpose: reveal the aptitude that the sect world will contest

beats.name: training under a master
beats.purpose: impose discipline, lineage, and a code the hero will be tested against

beats.name: first standing in the jianghu
beats.purpose: win a name in the martial world and its obligations

beats.name: sect politics and attachment
beats.purpose: entangle the hero in rivalries, debts, and love

beats.name: betrayal
beats.purpose: have a trusted figure destroy the hero's standing

beats.name: exile and injury
beats.purpose: strip skill, reputation, and allies together

beats.name: secret manual and breakthrough
beats.purpose: reach a higher level in isolation, at a physical or moral price

beats.name: return and reckoning
beats.purpose: reappear and dismantle the betrayer's position

beats.name: the final duel
beats.purpose: settle the debt in single combat governed by the code

beats.name: withdrawal from the jianghu
beats.purpose: leave the martial world rather than rule it

mythic_journeys.register: wuxia and xianxia fiction, martial-arts film; kin to the revenge and mastery plots
mythic_journeys.caution: The retreat at the end is the genre's moral position on power; ending on the throne instead turns a wuxia into an empire story.

classical_and_world.name: freytag's pyramid
classical_and_world.definition: The five-part dramatic pyramid — introduction, rise, climax, return, catastrophe — hinged on an exciting force early and a moment of final suspense late.

beats.name: introduction
beats.purpose: set place, party, and the conditions of the conflict

beats.name: exciting force
beats.purpose: release the impulse that starts the rising movement

beats.name: rising movement
beats.purpose: build the protagonist's advantage through escalating scenes

beats.name: climax
beats.purpose: put the protagonist at the height of their power and the turn at its point

beats.name: tragic force and reversal
beats.purpose: release the counterforce that turns the movement downward

beats.name: falling movement
beats.purpose: run the consequences as the opposition takes the initiative

beats.name: moment of final suspense
beats.purpose: offer one last apparent chance of escape

beats.name: catastrophe
beats.purpose: complete the fall and discharge the tension

beats.name: denouement
beats.purpose: settle the survivors and close the frame

classical_and_world.register: five-act tragedy and classical drama; the ancestor of the school-taught plot diagram
classical_and_world.caution: Freytag was describing tragedy, where the climax sits at the middle and the fall follows; the modern habit of putting the climax at ninety percent is a different shape wearing his name.

classical_and_world.name: greek tragedy
classical_and_world.definition: The Attic sequence of choral and spoken sections — prologos, parodos, alternating episodes and stasima, exodos — organized around reversal, recognition, and suffering.

beats.name: prologos
beats.purpose: state the situation and the god or debt behind it

beats.name: parodos
beats.purpose: bring the chorus on and establish the community's stake

beats.name: first episode and stasimon
beats.purpose: set the protagonist's course and let the chorus weigh it

beats.name: second episode and stasimon
beats.purpose: harden the opposition and narrow the options

beats.name: peripeteia
beats.purpose: reverse the action so that the effort produces its opposite

beats.name: anagnorisis
beats.purpose: convert ignorance into knowledge, usually of kinship or guilt

beats.name: kommos
beats.purpose: let protagonist and chorus lament together

beats.name: pathos
beats.purpose: deliver the destructive act, reported rather than shown

beats.name: final stasimon
beats.purpose: give the chorus the general lesson the particular case supports

beats.name: exodos
beats.purpose: clear the stage and leave the audience purged

classical_and_world.register: verse drama, adaptation, and any narrative where a community must witness a fall
classical_and_world.caution: The chorus is a structural organ, not decoration; dropping it removes the audience's licensed reaction and the form's moral balance.

classical_and_world.name: old comedy structure
classical_and_world.definition: The Aristophanic sequence in which a fantastic scheme is proposed, formally debated in the agon, endorsed in the parabasis, and then played out in escalating comic episodes.

beats.name: prologos
beats.purpose: introduce an ordinary citizen with an absurd remedy for a public ill

beats.name: parodos
beats.purpose: bring on a hostile or curious chorus

beats.name: agon
beats.purpose: settle the scheme by formal debate between opposed positions

beats.name: parabasis
beats.purpose: step out of the fiction and address the audience directly

beats.name: first episodes
beats.purpose: run the consequences of the enacted scheme as satirical set pieces

beats.name: escalating episodes
beats.purpose: bring the scheme's victims on in worsening order

beats.name: climactic episode
beats.purpose: cap the sequence with the largest target

beats.name: exodos
beats.purpose: end in feast, song, or wedding regardless of logic

classical_and_world.register: satire, political comedy, sketch and revue writing
classical_and_world.caution: The episodes after the parabasis are deliberately non-causal; imposing a plot on them removes the satire's freedom to keep changing targets.

classical_and_world.name: roman new comedy
classical_and_world.definition: The Plautine and Terentian five-part shape — protasis, epitasis, catastrophe — in which a scheme by clever subordinates drives obstruction toward recognition and marriage.

beats.name: expository prologue
beats.purpose: tell the audience the secret the characters do not know

beats.name: the household in place
beats.purpose: introduce the lovers, the blocking figure, and the clever slave

beats.name: the scheme
beats.purpose: launch the deception intended to defeat the obstruction

beats.name: complications multiply
beats.purpose: let each patch on the deception require another

beats.name: crisis of the intrigue
beats.purpose: bring the scheme to the edge of collapse

beats.name: near-discovery
beats.purpose: escape exposure by improvisation and nerve

beats.name: recognition
beats.purpose: reveal the birth or identity that dissolves the obstruction

beats.name: reconciliation
beats.purpose: let the blocking figure accept what he cannot prevent

beats.name: marriage and resolution
beats.purpose: close on the union and the restored household

classical_and_world.register: farce, romantic comedy, sitcom; the ancestor of most comic plotting in English
classical_and_world.caution: The recognition token must be planted early; a birthmark produced in the last scene reads as authorial rescue rather than comic design.

classical_and_world.name: shakespearean five-act
classical_and_world.definition: The Elizabethan five-act working of the pyramid, with the turning point at the third act and a fourth act of consequences before the fifth-act settlement.

beats.name: exposition and atmosphere
beats.purpose: open on a public scene that sets tone and the state of the world

beats.name: the exciting force
beats.purpose: introduce the demand, prophecy, or love that sets the action

beats.name: commitment
beats.purpose: have the protagonist choose the course the play will test

beats.name: entanglement
beats.purpose: complicate with subplot, disguise, or misinformation

beats.name: turning point
beats.purpose: place the central act where fortune changes direction

beats.name: the aftermath
beats.purpose: let the consequences begin before anyone can adjust

beats.name: counterplay
beats.purpose: give the opposing force the initiative

beats.name: moment of final suspense
beats.purpose: raise the possibility of a different ending

beats.name: catastrophe or resolution
beats.purpose: settle the action in deaths or marriages

beats.name: restoration and closing address
beats.purpose: hand the world to a survivor and speak the last lines outward

classical_and_world.register: stage drama and adaptation; a useful chapter grouping for novels in five parts
classical_and_world.caution: The fourth act is where the form is usually lost — it is the consequences act, not a delay before the fifth.

classical_and_world.name: kishotenketsu
classical_and_world.definition: The four-part East Asian structure — ki, sho, ten, ketsu — in which interest comes from a turn that recontextualizes what preceded it rather than from conflict.

beats.name: ki: introduction
beats.purpose: present the situation and its people without opposition

beats.name: sho: development
beats.purpose: deepen and extend the situation on its own terms

beats.name: ten: the turn arrives
beats.purpose: introduce something that appears unrelated to everything so far

beats.name: ten: the connection seen
beats.purpose: reveal how the new element reframes the first two parts

beats.name: ketsu: reconciliation
beats.purpose: bring the reframed elements into harmony

beats.name: ketsu: closing image
beats.purpose: settle on an image that holds both readings at once

classical_and_world.register: literary fiction, manga, four-panel comics, contemplative and slice-of-life narrative
classical_and_world.caution: Four parts, six beats here: ten and ketsu are split so the turn and its recognition can be budgeted apart. Reading ten as a plot twist rebuilds the conflict structure the form exists without; the turn shifts perspective, it need not raise stakes.

classical_and_world.name: jo-ha-kyu
classical_and_world.definition: The Japanese three-phase modulation of tempo — slow beginning, breaking development, swift conclusion — applied fractally to a whole programme, a play, a scene, and a gesture.

beats.name: jo: the auspicious opening
beats.purpose: begin slowly and formally, withholding incident

beats.name: jo into ha: the first break
beats.purpose: let the regular surface admit its first irregularity

beats.name: ha: development
beats.purpose: break the established pattern and vary the tempo

beats.name: ha: intensification
beats.purpose: accelerate and complicate toward the point of maximum instability

beats.name: kyu: the swift conclusion
beats.purpose: resolve rapidly, in a fraction of the time the opening took

beats.name: the return to stillness
beats.purpose: stop on silence rather than on a summary

classical_and_world.register: Noh and kabuki, renga sequencing, martial arts, and any prose that wants pacing as a structural principle
classical_and_world.caution: The proportions are unequal by design — a kyu given a quarter of the running time is no longer a kyu.

classical_and_world.name: noh five-dan
classical_and_world.definition: Zeami's five-section play: a travelling witness meets a disguised spirit who tells a story, withdraws, and returns in true form to dance its essence before a final stillness.

beats.name: the witness arrives
beats.purpose: let the living traveller name himself, his origin, and his destination

beats.name: the travel song
beats.purpose: carry the audience to the charged place through poetry alone

beats.name: the disguised figure enters
beats.purpose: introduce the protagonist in ordinary form, unexplained

beats.name: question and answer
beats.purpose: draw the local legend out until the teller knows too much

beats.name: the narrative dance
beats.purpose: let chorus and restrained movement carry the story's grief

beats.name: the withdrawal
beats.purpose: admit the true identity and leave the stage to change

beats.name: return in true form
beats.purpose: reappear as ghost, god, or demon, fully manifest

beats.name: the climactic dance
beats.purpose: replace language with movement at the point of highest intensity

beats.name: the closing chant
beats.purpose: resolve or eternally suspend the spirit's condition

beats.name: the final stamp
beats.purpose: end on one decisive sound and then silence

classical_and_world.register: Noh drama; adaptable to ghost stories and any narrative built on a witness and a revenant
classical_and_world.caution: Nothing here is driven by a protagonist's goal; imported conflict destroys the form's central effect, which is contemplation of a fixed condition.

classical_and_world.name: sanskrit five sandhi
classical_and_world.definition: The Natyashastra's five junctures — mukha, pratimukha, garbha, avamarsha, nirvahana — through which a seed is planted, unfolded, sprouted, doubted, and brought to fruit under a governing rasa.

beats.name: benediction and preliminaries
beats.purpose: open with invocation and establish the performance frame

beats.name: mukha: planting the seed
beats.purpose: introduce the germ of the action and the desired end

beats.name: pratimukha: unfolding
beats.purpose: let the seed appear and disappear as the pursuit begins

beats.name: rasa deepening
beats.purpose: thicken the emotional texture with subordinate flavours

beats.name: garbha: sprouting
beats.purpose: make attainment visible but repeatedly deferred

beats.name: approaching certainty
beats.purpose: bring the goal within reach so that doubt can matter

beats.name: avamarsha: the pause of deliberation
beats.purpose: hold the action in doubt, temptation, or curse

beats.name: rasa climax
beats.purpose: let the dominant flavour reach full intensity

beats.name: nirvahana: convergence on the fruit
beats.purpose: gather every planted thread into the attainment

beats.name: aesthetic peace
beats.purpose: settle the emotion into tranquillity rather than triumph

beats.name: closing benediction
beats.purpose: return the audience to the world with a blessing

classical_and_world.register: Sanskrit drama and its descendants; useful wherever emotional flavour, not conflict, is the organizing principle
classical_and_world.caution: The junctures are named by what the seed is doing, not by rising tension; mapping them onto three acts loses the deliberation phase that gives the form its weight.

classical_and_world.name: propp's morphology
classical_and_world.definition: The recurring function sequence of the Russian wonder tale, condensed: an interdiction is violated, villainy creates a lack, the hero is dispatched, tested by a donor, and returns to unmask a false claimant.

beats.name: absentation and interdiction
beats.purpose: remove a protector and impose a prohibition

beats.name: violation
beats.purpose: break the prohibition and open the world to harm

beats.name: reconnaissance and trickery
beats.purpose: let the villain gather information and deceive

beats.name: villainy or lack
beats.purpose: inflict the harm or name the thing missing

beats.name: mediation and departure
beats.purpose: dispatch the hero, who agrees to counteraction

beats.name: the donor's test
beats.purpose: test the hero's manners or courage before granting aid

beats.name: receipt of the magical agent
beats.purpose: hand over the helper or object that makes victory possible

beats.name: guidance to the object
beats.purpose: transfer the hero to where the lack can be repaired

beats.name: struggle and branding
beats.purpose: join combat and mark the hero with a wound or token

beats.name: victory and liquidation of the lack
beats.purpose: defeat the villain and restore what was missing

beats.name: pursuit and rescue
beats.purpose: flee the counterattack by cunning or transformation

beats.name: unrecognized arrival
beats.purpose: return home unknown

beats.name: false claim and difficult task
beats.purpose: let an impostor claim the deed and set a final test

beats.name: recognition and exposure
beats.purpose: identify the hero by the mark and unmask the impostor

beats.name: punishment and transfiguration
beats.purpose: punish the villain and remake the hero's appearance or station

beats.name: wedding and accession
beats.purpose: close on marriage, throne, or both

classical_and_world.aka: Propp's functions, morphology of the folktale
classical_and_world.register: folk tale, fairy tale, and structural analysis; a generator as well as a description
classical_and_world.caution: Propp's claim is that functions keep their order, not that all appear; using all thirty-one produces a pastiche no folk tale ever was.

classical_and_world.name: fichtean curve
classical_and_world.definition: A crisis-dense shape that opens in motion and stacks escalating crises, each raising tension higher than the last, until a late climax and a very short fall.

beats.name: opening in motion
beats.purpose: start inside trouble and explain nothing yet

beats.name: first crisis
beats.purpose: establish the pattern: pressure, response, worse position

beats.name: response and complication
beats.purpose: supply the backstory in the gaps between crises

beats.name: second crisis
beats.purpose: raise the cost and remove an option

beats.name: third crisis
beats.purpose: take away a support the protagonist counted on

beats.name: fourth crisis
beats.purpose: push to the near-breaking point

beats.name: reckoning
beats.purpose: force the choice the accumulated crises have been shaping

beats.name: climax
beats.purpose: resolve at the highest point of the stack

beats.name: brief falling action
beats.purpose: release tension quickly; the form does not linger

beats.name: new equilibrium
beats.purpose: state the changed condition in a few lines

classical_and_world.register: thriller, horror, action, and serialized fiction that cannot afford a slow opening
classical_and_world.caution: Without troughs between crises the reader goes numb; the curve rises overall but must still dip after each peak.

classical_and_world.name: homeric epic structure
classical_and_world.definition: The epic sequence: invocation, opening in the middle of things, catalogue and assembly, divine interference, aristeia, a descent, and a homecoming.

beats.name: invocation
beats.purpose: name the subject and ask the muse for it

beats.name: beginning in the middle
beats.purpose: enter at the crisis, not the origin

beats.name: assembly and quarrel
beats.purpose: set the human conflict among leaders

beats.name: catalogue
beats.purpose: enumerate the forces and give the world its scale

beats.name: divine intervention
beats.purpose: let a god tilt the human situation

beats.name: exploits and trials
beats.purpose: run the episodes that prove and test the hero

beats.name: aristeia
beats.purpose: give the hero a stretch of unmatched excellence

beats.name: the descent
beats.purpose: consult the dead and learn what the living cannot say

beats.name: divine council and turn
beats.purpose: settle the outcome above before it happens below

beats.name: the supreme trial
beats.purpose: stage the confrontation the whole poem has deferred

beats.name: homecoming
beats.purpose: restore or fail to restore the hero to a household

classical_and_world.register: epic poetry and its prose descendants; also a template for large ensemble fantasy
classical_and_world.caution: The catalogue and the divine council are what make the scale felt; cutting them for pace turns an epic into a long adventure novel.

classical_and_world.name: grimm fairy-tale pattern
classical_and_world.definition: The household folk-tale shape: a prohibition, a departure into the forest, a magical helper, three trials, and a settlement in which reward and punishment are both literal.

beats.name: once upon a time
beats.purpose: state family, poverty, or lack in a single sentence

beats.name: prohibition
beats.purpose: issue the warning the tale exists to break

beats.name: violation and expulsion
beats.purpose: break the rule and lose the safety of home

beats.name: into the forest
beats.purpose: cross into the place where the rules are magical

beats.name: the helper
beats.purpose: reward simple kindness with disproportionate aid

beats.name: three trials
beats.purpose: test the protagonist three times, hardest last

beats.name: confrontation
beats.purpose: defeat the witch, wolf, or stepmother by wit or nerve

beats.name: reward and punishment
beats.purpose: distribute both without mercy or ambiguity

beats.name: transformation restored
beats.purpose: return the enchanted to their true shapes

beats.name: happily ever after
beats.purpose: close the frame with marriage, plenty, or safety

classical_and_world.register: fairy tale, children's fiction, and adult retellings that trade on the pattern
classical_and_world.caution: The flat affect is the form: psychology stated rather than dramatized. Adding interiority is a legitimate retelling but it is no longer this structure.

classical_and_world.name: aesop's fable
classical_and_world.definition: The minimal moral tale: a situation, an encounter, an action taken in character, an outcome that follows necessarily, and a stated moral.

beats.name: situation
beats.purpose: name two creatures and the condition between them

beats.name: encounter
beats.purpose: bring them into contact over a single want

beats.name: the action
beats.purpose: let each act exactly as their nature requires

beats.name: outcome
beats.purpose: deliver the consequence without mercy or delay

beats.name: the moral
beats.purpose: state the general rule the case illustrates

classical_and_world.register: fable, parable, and the opening exercise of the classical rhetorical curriculum
classical_and_world.caution: The moral must be derivable from the action; if the tag line supplies information the story withheld, the fable has failed as an argument.

classical_and_world.name: ring composition
classical_and_world.definition: A symmetrical arrangement in which elements introduced on the way in are answered in reverse order on the way out, around a central pivot that carries the meaning.

beats.name: outer frame opens
beats.purpose: state the terms and the occasion that will be returned to

beats.name: first element
beats.purpose: introduce the motif that the last movement will answer

beats.name: second element
beats.purpose: layer the next term inward, marked so it can be recognized again

beats.name: approach to the centre
beats.purpose: narrow toward the turn with the innermost material

beats.name: the pivot
beats.purpose: place the story's argument or revelation at the exact centre

beats.name: second element answered
beats.purpose: return the innermost term transformed by the pivot

beats.name: first element answered
beats.purpose: answer the earlier motif in reverse order

beats.name: outer frame closes
beats.purpose: return to the opening terms with their meaning changed

classical_and_world.register: oral epic, scripture, essay, and literary fiction that rewards rereading
classical_and_world.caution: Symmetry has to be perceptible without a diagram; if only the author can find the ring, it is decoration rather than structure.

genre_sheets.name: whodunit mystery
genre_sheets.definition: The fair-play detective structure: a crime, an investigator engaged, a field of suspects with means and motive, a misdirected middle, and a solution the reader could have reached.

beats.name: the world before the crime
beats.purpose: show the closed community and plant every later clue in plain sight

beats.name: the body
beats.purpose: commit the crime and freeze the situation the plot will thaw

beats.name: the detective engaged
beats.purpose: bring in the investigator and their reason to care

beats.name: first canvass
beats.purpose: collect testimony that is mostly true and partly self-serving

beats.name: false leads
beats.purpose: let a plausible theory absorb the reader's attention

beats.name: interviews and alibis
beats.purpose: narrow the field while giving each suspect a defensible story

beats.name: the crucial detail
beats.purpose: place the decisive fact where it can be seen and not understood

beats.name: second crime
beats.purpose: escalate by removing whoever was about to speak

beats.name: the wrong arrest
beats.purpose: let the official theory take hold and be wrong

beats.name: the reversal
beats.purpose: have the detective see the pattern the reader has been given

beats.name: the confrontation
beats.purpose: gather the suspects and reconstruct the crime aloud

beats.name: denouement
beats.purpose: settle guilt, motive, and what the community will do next

genre_sheets.register: crime fiction, cosy and golden-age forms, procedural television
genre_sheets.caution: Fair play is structural, not decorative: every clue used in the solution must have been available, and withholding one converts a mystery into a trick.

genre_sheets.name: inverted detective story
genre_sheets.definition: The howdunit: the crime and criminal are shown first, and the tension comes from watching an investigator close on a mistake the audience already knows about.

beats.name: the plan
beats.purpose: let the audience watch the murderer prepare in full

beats.name: the crime committed
beats.purpose: execute the plan, including the one imperfect element

beats.name: the cover
beats.purpose: establish the alibi the rest of the story will erode

beats.name: the investigator arrives
beats.purpose: introduce the detective and their apparent harmlessness

beats.name: first snag
beats.purpose: let the detective notice the flaw the audience is watching for

beats.name: pressure and improvisation
beats.purpose: force the criminal into new lies that create new evidence

beats.name: the second mistake
beats.purpose: make the cover-up more incriminating than the crime

beats.name: the trap
beats.purpose: have the detective stage a situation only the guilty would react to

beats.name: confession
beats.purpose: close with the criminal's recognition rather than the reader's

genre_sheets.register: crime television and fiction; dramatic irony in place of puzzle
genre_sheets.caution: The pleasure is the criminal's competence eroding, so the detective must never look lucky — every step needs an inference the audience can check.

genre_sheets.name: heist caper
genre_sheets.definition: The crew structure: an impossible target, a team assembled by specialism, a plan shown to the audience, execution that goes wrong, and a reveal that the failure was the plan.

beats.name: the operator's situation
beats.purpose: establish the leader's skill and their reason to need this job

beats.name: the target
beats.purpose: present the score and the security that makes it impossible

beats.name: assembling the crew
beats.purpose: introduce each specialist by the problem they solve

beats.name: casing
beats.purpose: gather the constraints the plan will have to satisfy

beats.name: the plan
beats.purpose: show the audience a version of the plan, complete and confident

beats.name: preparation
beats.purpose: rehearse, build, and expose the crew's frictions

beats.name: the wild card
beats.purpose: change one condition after the plan is locked

beats.name: the job begins
beats.purpose: run the first phase exactly as promised

beats.name: complications
beats.purpose: break the plan in ways that force improvisation on the clock

beats.name: the double-cross
beats.purpose: have someone inside the crew act against it

beats.name: the reveal
beats.purpose: show the hidden layer that reframes everything just watched

beats.name: the split
beats.purpose: distribute the take and the consequences

genre_sheets.register: crime film and fiction; also the shape of many con and prison-break stories
genre_sheets.caution: The reveal must use only material the audience saw; a hidden accomplice introduced in the last five minutes cheats the contract the plan sequence made.

genre_sheets.name: romance beat sheet
genre_sheets.definition: The genre's obligatory arc: two people meet, are forced together, fall in love against internal resistance, break under the flaw that resistance protected, and choose each other with the flaw surrendered.

beats.name: both lives before
beats.purpose: show each protagonist's wound and what it costs them daily

beats.name: the meeting
beats.purpose: bring them together in a way that charges the room

beats.name: attraction and denial
beats.purpose: establish the reason each refuses what they feel

beats.name: the adhesion
beats.purpose: impose a reason they cannot simply walk away

beats.name: growing connection
beats.purpose: let intimacy accumulate through small, specific concessions

beats.name: the turning point
beats.purpose: cross a line — a kiss, a confession — that changes the terms

beats.name: midpoint commitment
beats.purpose: give them the relationship, briefly, at full intensity

beats.name: retreat
beats.purpose: let the old wound reassert itself against the new closeness

beats.name: the black moment
beats.purpose: break them apart over the thing neither would surrender

beats.name: dark night
beats.purpose: leave each alone with what the loss reveals

beats.name: the grand gesture
beats.purpose: have one act publicly against their own defence

beats.name: the resolution
beats.purpose: deliver the union the genre promised, with the cost paid

genre_sheets.aka: courtship arc, the romance obligatory scenes
genre_sheets.register: romance in all subgenres; the emotionally satisfying ending is a genre contract, not a choice
genre_sheets.caution: The black moment must come from the flaw established in act one — a misunderstanding a single sentence would clear reads as manufactured and breaks the reader's trust.

genre_sheets.name: horror escalation
genre_sheets.definition: The ratchet: normality, an anomaly explained away, escalation past deniability, isolation, false victory, and a resolution that leaves the threat's logic intact.

beats.name: false normalcy
beats.purpose: establish an ordinary life worth being afraid for

beats.name: the first sign
beats.purpose: introduce an anomaly small enough to dismiss

beats.name: rational explanation
beats.purpose: let a character explain it away convincingly

beats.name: escalation
beats.purpose: repeat the anomaly at a scale that defeats the explanation

beats.name: point of no return
beats.purpose: cut off the exit that would have ended the story

beats.name: isolation
beats.purpose: remove help, communication, and disbelieving allies

beats.name: learning the rules
beats.purpose: let the survivors work out what the threat can and cannot do

beats.name: false victory
beats.purpose: appear to defeat or escape it

beats.name: full confrontation
beats.purpose: meet the thing on its own terms with the real cost

beats.name: desperate measures
beats.purpose: survive by sacrificing something that mattered

beats.name: the lingering dread
beats.purpose: close on the sign that the rules still hold

genre_sheets.register: horror across media; the sequence is closer to a tension schedule than a plot
genre_sheets.caution: Every escalation must cost the characters an option; repetition without narrowing produces boredom, which is fatal to fear.

genre_sheets.name: redemption plot
genre_sheets.definition: The arc from a committed wrong to earned restoration: consequences, rock bottom, a catalyst, incremental atonement, a relapse test, and a sacrificial act that pays the original debt.

beats.name: the wrong
beats.purpose: establish the act, with the harm shown rather than described

beats.name: living with it
beats.purpose: show the self-justification that keeps the character functional

beats.name: rock bottom
beats.purpose: take away the last thing the justification was protecting

beats.name: the catalyst
beats.purpose: offer a specific chance to act differently

beats.name: first steps
beats.purpose: let small restitutions be refused or unnoticed

beats.name: temptation to relapse
beats.purpose: make the old life available again on easy terms

beats.name: test of the new values
beats.purpose: force a choice where honesty costs materially

beats.name: acceptance withheld
beats.purpose: let the wronged party refuse to forgive on schedule

beats.name: the sacrifice
beats.purpose: pay a price commensurate with the original harm

beats.name: the new life
beats.purpose: grant restoration that is partial and hard-won

genre_sheets.register: literary and genre fiction, drama; often the antagonist's arc in an ensemble
genre_sheets.caution: Forgiveness granted by the victim on cue is the failure mode; redemption is measured by what the character surrenders, not by who absolves them.

genre_sheets.name: corruption plot
genre_sheets.definition: The inverse arc: a decent person meets a pressure, makes a defensible first compromise, is rewarded for it, and descends by increments until the original self is unrecoverable.

beats.name: the good position
beats.purpose: establish the principle and the person who holds it

beats.name: the pressure
beats.purpose: apply a need that the principle cannot meet

beats.name: first compromise
beats.purpose: cross a small line for a good reason

beats.name: rationalization
beats.purpose: build the story that makes the crossing sensible

beats.name: reward
beats.purpose: let the compromise pay, publicly

beats.name: deeper compromise
beats.purpose: raise the price and let the character pay it faster

beats.name: the warning
beats.purpose: have someone who loves them name what is happening

beats.name: severing
beats.purpose: cut the relationship that would have stopped the descent

beats.name: point of no return
beats.purpose: commit an act with no defensible reading

beats.name: full descent
beats.purpose: operate entirely by the new logic, competently

beats.name: destruction
beats.purpose: let the consequences arrive without redemption

genre_sheets.register: tragedy, crime drama, literary fiction; the standard shape of the antihero series
genre_sheets.caution: Each step must be defensible when taken, or the character is not corrupted but merely revealed — a different, weaker story.

genre_sheets.name: revenge tragedy
genre_sheets.definition: The Elizabethan pattern: a wrong beyond legal remedy, a revelation, a vow, delay filled with scheming and feigned madness, and a bloody climax that consumes the avenger.

beats.name: the wrong
beats.purpose: commit an injury the law cannot or will not address

beats.name: the revelation
beats.purpose: disclose the crime to the avenger, often by a ghost or document

beats.name: the vow
beats.purpose: bind the avenger to a course with a formal promise

beats.name: scheming and delay
beats.purpose: postpone the act while gathering proof and opportunity

beats.name: madness, real or feigned
beats.purpose: let the mask of derangement license truth-telling

beats.name: the device
beats.purpose: spring a play, letter, or trap that confirms the guilt publicly

beats.name: moral deterioration
beats.purpose: have the avenger harm the innocent in service of the vow

beats.name: the counterplot
beats.purpose: let the guilty move first and force the timetable

beats.name: the bloodbath
beats.purpose: settle everything in a single accelerating catastrophe

beats.name: the avenger falls
beats.purpose: kill the avenger with the same machinery

beats.name: restoration of order
beats.purpose: let an outsider take the stage and count the bodies

genre_sheets.aka: the revenge play, Senecan revenge structure
genre_sheets.register: tragedy, noir, and the modern vengeance thriller
genre_sheets.caution: The delay is the form's subject; removing it produces an efficient thriller with none of the moral cost that makes revenge tragedy tragic.

genre_sheets.name: sports underdog
genre_sheets.definition: The competitive arc: an overlooked contender gets one chance, trains, wins early, is set back, recommits for a reason larger than winning, and meets the favourite at full strength.

beats.name: the overlooked life
beats.purpose: establish the talent and the circumstances wasting it

beats.name: the opportunity
beats.purpose: offer a shot that should not be available

beats.name: reluctant commitment
beats.purpose: let the fear of hoping be the real obstacle

beats.name: the coach and the code
beats.purpose: impose a discipline that is also a moral position

beats.name: training
beats.purpose: show the unglamorous work in compressed, specific detail

beats.name: first competition
beats.purpose: win enough to make the ambition public and irreversible

beats.name: setback
beats.purpose: take away the body, the team, or the mentor

beats.name: the dark moment
beats.purpose: let the contender quit in a way that costs someone else

beats.name: recommitment
beats.purpose: return for a reason that is not the trophy

beats.name: the big game
beats.purpose: stage the contest with the opposition at their honest best

beats.name: victory or moral victory
beats.purpose: settle the outer result and the inner one separately

genre_sheets.register: sports film and fiction; transfers to any skill-mastery story, from music to law
genre_sheets.caution: If the ending needs the trophy to work, the inner arc was never load-bearing; the strongest versions can survive losing the match.

genre_sheets.name: war story
genre_sheets.definition: The soldier's arc: enlistment and training, the first contact that ends abstraction, attrition and the loss of the group, a mission with a cost, and a homecoming into a world that cannot hear it.

beats.name: life before
beats.purpose: show the peace and the belief that will not survive

beats.name: the call to service
beats.purpose: give a reason for going that the story will interrogate

beats.name: training and the group
beats.purpose: forge the unit whose members will be spent

beats.name: deployment
beats.purpose: arrive at the place where the rules are different

beats.name: first combat
beats.purpose: replace the idea of war with the fact of it

beats.name: loss of innocence
beats.purpose: kill the first member of the group or the first civilian

beats.name: attrition
beats.purpose: grind the unit down between engagements

beats.name: the mission
beats.purpose: assign an objective whose value is questionable and whose cost is not

beats.name: the worst of it
beats.purpose: put the protagonist past what they believed they would do

beats.name: sacrifice
beats.purpose: spend a life for something the story refuses to price

beats.name: the objective settled
beats.purpose: achieve or lose the mission, anticlimactically

beats.name: homecoming
beats.purpose: return to a peace that has no vocabulary for it

genre_sheets.register: war fiction, film, and memoir; the homecoming beat is what separates it from the mission thriller
genre_sheets.caution: The genre's moral risk runs both ways: an arc that ends in glory falsifies the middle, one that ends only in horror can flatten the people it depicts.

genre_sheets.name: survival story
genre_sheets.definition: Human against circumstance: a catastrophe, inventory and improvisation, psychological collapse, adaptation, an escape attempt, and a return carrying what the ordeal changed.

beats.name: normal life
beats.purpose: establish competence and dependence on infrastructure

beats.name: the catastrophe
beats.purpose: remove the infrastructure in a single event

beats.name: shock
beats.purpose: spend the first hours doing the wrong things

beats.name: inventory
beats.purpose: count what exists and convert panic into problems

beats.name: first solutions
beats.purpose: solve water, warmth, or shelter and buy time

beats.name: the new threat
beats.purpose: introduce a second-order danger the first solution created

beats.name: psychological crisis
beats.purpose: let isolation and time do what the environment could not

beats.name: the anchor
beats.purpose: supply a companion, ritual, or object that holds the mind together

beats.name: adaptation
beats.purpose: show real skill acquired, and the person changed by acquiring it

beats.name: the attempt
beats.purpose: stake everything on one route out

beats.name: the final trial
beats.purpose: impose a last cost that the earlier version could not have paid

beats.name: return
beats.purpose: reach other people and find the ordeal untranslatable

genre_sheets.register: survival fiction and film, disaster narrative, adventure memoir
genre_sheets.caution: Competence porn without deterioration is a procedure; the psychological crisis is what makes the practical detail matter.

genre_sheets.name: courtroom drama
genre_sheets.definition: The trial structure: an injustice, an advocate who takes the case for a reason, discovery and pressure, the trial's set pieces, a late reversal in evidence, and a verdict that settles less than expected.

beats.name: the injustice
beats.purpose: commit the act and fix the audience's sense of what is true

beats.name: the accused
beats.purpose: introduce a client who is sympathetic, unsympathetic, or both

beats.name: taking the case
beats.purpose: give the advocate a personal reason and a professional cost

beats.name: discovery
beats.purpose: gather facts that complicate the initial certainty

beats.name: building the theory
beats.purpose: commit to the story the trial will have to sustain

beats.name: pressure outside the record
beats.purpose: threaten the advocate's practice, family, or licence

beats.name: pre-trial rulings
beats.purpose: decide what the jury will never hear

beats.name: the trial opens
beats.purpose: state both theories to the jury and start the clock

beats.name: cross-examination
beats.purpose: break or fail to break the opposing witness on the record

beats.name: the late reversal
beats.purpose: produce evidence or a witness that changes the theory mid-trial

beats.name: closing arguments
beats.purpose: make the moral case that the legal case only approximates

beats.name: verdict and aftermath
beats.purpose: deliver the ruling and show what it did not fix

genre_sheets.register: legal fiction, film and television; the beats survive translation into inquiry, tribunal, and hearing stories
genre_sheets.caution: Real procedure is the source of the tension, so invented rules cost credibility; the surprise witness is a genre convention that most jurisdictions would not permit.

genre_sheets.name: bildungsroman arc
genre_sheets.definition: The formation novel: a young protagonist is wounded, leaves home, is educated by mentors and loves, collides with society, suffers disillusionment, and reaches an accommodation with the world.

beats.name: the childhood world
beats.purpose: establish the given self before anything has tested it

beats.name: the wound
beats.purpose: impose the loss or shame that starts the formation

beats.name: departure
beats.purpose: leave home for the city, the school, or the trade

beats.name: education
beats.purpose: supply mentors, books, and their competing accounts of life

beats.name: first love
beats.purpose: attach the self to another person and misjudge it

beats.name: collision with society
beats.purpose: meet the class, money, or power that will not yield

beats.name: crisis of identity
beats.purpose: let every borrowed model of the self fail at once

beats.name: disillusionment
beats.purpose: strip the ambition down to what is actually available

beats.name: the mature choice
beats.purpose: choose a life on terms the protagonist now understands

beats.name: return or integration
beats.purpose: revisit the origin from the far side of formation

genre_sheets.register: literary fiction and memoir; the dominant shape of the first novel
