genre_sheets.caution: Episodes of growth need a through-line of desire, or the book becomes a chronology; the reader must know what the protagonist is trying to become.

genre_sheets.name: noir descent
genre_sheets.definition: The hardboiled shape: a compromised protagonist takes a small job, finds a larger corruption, is entangled by desire, betrays or is betrayed, and wins at a cost that is not worth it.

beats.name: the narrator's world
beats.purpose: establish a voice that already knows how this ends

beats.name: the client
beats.purpose: bring in the job with a lie inside it

beats.name: the small case
beats.purpose: start on something ordinary and slightly unpleasant

beats.name: the wider rot
beats.purpose: trace the case upward into institutional corruption

beats.name: entanglement
beats.purpose: let desire compromise the protagonist's judgement

beats.name: the beating
beats.purpose: have power demonstrate itself physically

beats.name: betrayal
beats.purpose: reveal that the client or the lover was running the protagonist

beats.name: moral compromise
beats.purpose: force the protagonist to do something they cannot excuse

beats.name: the trap
beats.purpose: close the frame around them with the evidence pointing their way

beats.name: violent resolution
beats.purpose: settle it with violence that fixes nothing structural

beats.name: pyrrhic ending
beats.purpose: leave the protagonist alive, correct, and worse off

genre_sheets.register: crime fiction and film noir; the voice is part of the structure, not a garnish
genre_sheets.caution: The corruption must be systemic for the ending to land; a single villain who can be arrested turns noir into a procedural.

genre_sheets.name: western showdown
genre_sheets.definition: The frontier structure: a stranger with a past arrives where law has failed, refuses the fight, is forced to it by an outrage, prepares, and settles it in a duel before leaving.

beats.name: arrival
beats.purpose: bring the stranger into a town with a problem

beats.name: the threat established
beats.purpose: show the power that the law cannot touch

beats.name: refusal
beats.purpose: have the stranger decline to be the town's solution

beats.name: the townspeople
beats.purpose: sort the community into the brave, the bought, and the frightened

beats.name: provocations
beats.purpose: escalate the pressure through small humiliations

beats.name: the outrage
beats.purpose: cross a line that makes refusal impossible

beats.name: the past surfaces
beats.purpose: reveal why the stranger stopped doing this

beats.name: preparation
beats.purpose: clean the weapon, set the ground, send the innocents away

beats.name: the showdown
beats.purpose: settle it face to face, quickly

beats.name: departure
beats.purpose: leave, because the town has no place for what fixed it

genre_sheets.aka: the frontier structure, the gunfighter arc
genre_sheets.register: westerns and their transpositions into science fiction, crime, and samurai film
genre_sheets.caution: The departure is the genre's argument about violence; letting the gunfighter settle down is a deliberate revision, not a variation.

genre_sheets.name: superhero origin
genre_sheets.definition: The powered-transformation arc: an ordinary person acquires ability, misuses or fumbles it, learns a code through loss, meets a villain who mirrors them, fails, and accepts the role.

beats.name: the ordinary person
beats.purpose: establish the powerlessness the powers will answer

beats.name: the transformative event
beats.purpose: grant the ability without consent or instruction

beats.name: discovery
beats.purpose: test the limits comically and privately

beats.name: selfish first use
beats.purpose: use the gift for personal gain

beats.name: the defining loss
beats.purpose: let that use cost someone the hero loved

beats.name: the code
beats.purpose: convert the loss into a rule the story will test

beats.name: first victory
beats.purpose: act publicly and be recognized as a symbol

beats.name: the villain emerges
beats.purpose: introduce an antagonist with the same power and no code

beats.name: the fall
beats.purpose: have the villain beat the hero and expose the private identity

beats.name: rising again
beats.purpose: return by choice, with the cost understood

beats.name: the final battle
beats.purpose: win by holding the code the villain abandoned

beats.name: accepting the mantle
beats.purpose: take on the permanent burden of the role

genre_sheets.register: comics, superhero film, and any narrative about the acquisition of dangerous capability
genre_sheets.caution: The mirrored villain is what makes the code an argument; an antagonist with unrelated powers reduces the climax to a fight.

episodic_and_frame.name: rashomon structure
episodic_and_frame.definition: The contested-event structure: one incident narrated in incompatible versions by interested parties, with the frame refusing to certify any of them.

beats.name: the frame
beats.purpose: gather the tellers and establish why the account matters now

beats.name: the event named
beats.purpose: state the bare facts everyone agrees on, and no more

beats.name: first account
beats.purpose: give the most authoritative version and let it convince

beats.name: second account
beats.purpose: contradict the first on a detail that changes the moral weight

beats.name: third account
beats.purpose: complicate both by reframing motive rather than fact

beats.name: the account no one can dismiss
beats.purpose: add the version that makes every teller look self-serving

beats.name: confrontation of accounts
beats.purpose: set the versions against each other in the frame

beats.name: the gesture
beats.purpose: settle the theme with an act rather than an adjudication

beats.name: the frame closes
beats.purpose: return to the tellers, leaving the fact undecided

episodic_and_frame.register: literary fiction, courtroom and journalism narratives, television episodes about memory
episodic_and_frame.caution: Every version must be internally coherent and self-flattering in a different way; versions that differ only in detail read as an error, not an epistemology.

episodic_and_frame.name: arabian nights frame
episodic_and_frame.definition: The nested tale-cycle: a frame in which telling stories staves off a threat, and interior tales that are broken at their peaks so the frame's danger renews each night.

beats.name: the frame's wound
beats.purpose: establish the injury that made the listener dangerous

beats.name: the teller's gambit
beats.purpose: let the storyteller volunteer, with a plan

beats.name: first tale opens
beats.purpose: hook the listener with a world unlike the frame's

beats.name: the tale deepens
beats.purpose: complicate the interior story and nest a tale inside it

beats.name: the interior crucible
beats.purpose: put the inner protagonist to a moral test that speaks to the frame

beats.name: the break
beats.purpose: stop at the peak; the listener must grant another night

beats.name: return to the frame
beats.purpose: show the listener changed by what he wanted to hear next

beats.name: later tales as argument
beats.purpose: let the sequence of stories make the case the teller cannot make directly

beats.name: the frame's transformation
beats.purpose: have the listener's own judgement shift

beats.name: release
beats.purpose: resolve the frame's threat by the accumulated effect of the telling

episodic_and_frame.register: story collections, novels-in-tales, and any narrative where the act of telling is the plot
episodic_and_frame.caution: The interior tales must bear on the frame's danger; a frame that merely introduces unrelated stories is packaging, and the reader stops caring about the outer level.

episodic_and_frame.name: epistolary sequence
episodic_and_frame.definition: A narrative told entirely in documents, where character comes from voice, plot from what correspondents withhold, and crisis from silences and intercepted texts.

beats.name: the first document
beats.purpose: establish voice, addressee, and the reason to write at all

beats.name: the correspondent answers
beats.purpose: open the second voice and let the two accounts diverge

beats.name: intimacy through writing
beats.purpose: let the letters do what the writers cannot do in person

beats.name: a third source
beats.purpose: introduce a document neither writer intended the other to see

beats.name: unreliability surfaces
beats.purpose: make the reader notice what a writer is shaping

beats.name: the crisis letter
beats.purpose: write the letter that cannot be unwritten

beats.name: the silence
beats.purpose: leave a gap in the correspondence and let the reader fill it

beats.name: the document from outside
beats.purpose: supply the report, clipping, or entry that settles the facts

beats.name: the resolving letter
beats.purpose: answer the crisis from the far side of the silence

beats.name: the last page
beats.purpose: close with an editorial note, a burnt letter, or an unanswered one

episodic_and_frame.aka: epistolary novel, documentary structure, found-document narrative
episodic_and_frame.register: literary fiction, horror, historical fiction; the modern forms substitute emails, transcripts, and case files
episodic_and_frame.caution: The form's constraint is that nothing can be narrated by someone who would not have written it down; every convenient document weakens the rest.

episodic_and_frame.name: try-fail escalation
episodic_and_frame.definition: A middle built as a chain of attempts, each ending in 'yes, but' or 'no, and', so that failure produces information and a narrower next attempt.

beats.name: the promise
beats.purpose: state the goal and the terms of success clearly enough to fail against

beats.name: the obvious attempt
beats.purpose: try what any competent person would try first

beats.name: yes, but
beats.purpose: grant the objective and attach a complication that costs more

beats.name: regroup
beats.purpose: let the character reinterpret the problem with the new information

beats.name: no, and
beats.purpose: deny the objective and take away a resource as well

beats.name: reassessment at the midpoint
beats.purpose: change the goal itself, not just the method

beats.name: the costly attempt
beats.purpose: succeed at a price that damages the character's position

beats.name: crisis
beats.purpose: leave only options that violate something the character values

beats.name: the earned attempt
beats.purpose: use everything the failures taught, and nothing else

beats.name: payoff
beats.purpose: show what the sequence of failures actually bought

episodic_and_frame.register: any plot-driven fiction; the standard remedy for a sagging second act
episodic_and_frame.caution: Attempts that fail for the same reason twice read as stalling; each failure must change what the character knows or has.

episodic_and_frame.name: scene and sequel loop
episodic_and_frame.definition: Dwight Swain's alternation: a scene of goal, conflict and disaster, followed by a sequel of reaction, dilemma and decision that generates the next scene's goal.

beats.name: scene: goal
beats.purpose: give the viewpoint character a specific, immediate objective

beats.name: scene: conflict
beats.purpose: oppose the objective with something that pushes back in real time

beats.name: scene: disaster
beats.purpose: end on a setback that changes the situation, not a stalemate

beats.name: sequel: reaction
beats.purpose: let the emotional response land before the thinking starts

beats.name: sequel: dilemma
beats.purpose: lay out options that are all bad in different ways

beats.name: sequel: decision
beats.purpose: choose, and thereby set the next scene's goal

beats.name: scene: escalated goal
beats.purpose: pursue the new objective at higher exposure

beats.name: scene: major reversal
beats.purpose: deliver a disaster that invalidates the strategy

beats.name: sequel: dark reflection
beats.purpose: run reaction and dilemma at their deepest point

beats.name: sequel: desperate commitment
beats.purpose: decide on the option that was previously unacceptable

beats.name: scene: final confrontation
beats.purpose: put goal and opposition in the same room for the last time

beats.name: closing sequel
beats.purpose: process the outcome and settle the new equilibrium

episodic_and_frame.register: commercial novel drafting; a rhythm rather than a plot, applied at any scale
episodic_and_frame.caution: All scene and no sequel exhausts the reader; all sequel and no scene stops the book. The proportion, not the pattern, is where drafts go wrong.

episodic_and_frame.name: picaresque episode chain
episodic_and_frame.definition: The rogue's chronicle: a low-born survivor moves from master to master, each episode a self-contained satire, with no transformation and no real ending.

beats.name: humble origins
beats.purpose: establish birth, hunger, and the absence of protection

beats.name: departure and first master
beats.purpose: enter service and learn the world's first lesson in cruelty

beats.name: survival by wit
beats.purpose: let the rogue cheat successfully and enjoy it

beats.name: the next master
beats.purpose: change social station and satirize a new institution

beats.name: the middle episodes
beats.purpose: run interchangeable adventures whose order barely matters

beats.name: brush with respectability
beats.purpose: offer a settled life on terms the rogue cannot keep

beats.name: exposure
beats.purpose: let the imposture collapse publicly

beats.name: reflection without reform
beats.purpose: have the rogue draw a moral they will not act on

beats.name: the open ending
beats.purpose: stop rather than conclude, with the road still running

episodic_and_frame.register: satire, comic novel, and road narrative
episodic_and_frame.caution: The absence of an arc is the form's argument about society; adding a redemption ending converts it into a bildungsroman and loses the satire.

episodic_and_frame.name: case-of-the-week season arc
episodic_and_frame.definition: The episodic-serial braid: a self-contained case resolved each installment, threaded with a season-long mythology that surfaces in a minority of episodes and pays off at the finale.

beats.name: premise pilot
beats.purpose: establish the team, the format, and the season's buried question

beats.name: format episodes
beats.purpose: run standalone cases that teach the audience the show's rules

beats.name: first mythology episode
beats.purpose: reveal that the weekly cases share a cause

beats.name: the runner deepens
beats.purpose: let the serial thread cost a character something personal

beats.name: midseason turn
beats.purpose: change the status quo so the format cannot continue unaltered

beats.name: cases under new conditions
beats.purpose: run the weekly form with the serial pressure inside it

beats.name: the betrayal
beats.purpose: expose an insider and break the team's assumptions

beats.name: penultimate escalation
beats.purpose: put the season's antagonist directly in front of the protagonists

beats.name: finale
beats.purpose: resolve the season question with a permanent consequence

beats.name: the hook for next season
beats.purpose: open a new question in the last minute

episodic_and_frame.register: network and streaming television; also serialized fiction and web serials
episodic_and_frame.caution: The mythology must be resolvable; strung out without answers, the audience learns that the serial thread is not a promise but a stall.

episodic_and_frame.name: telenovela closed arc
episodic_and_frame.definition: The finite melodrama: a love across a class divide, obstructed by a secret of birth and an active schemer, driven by weekly reversals to a fixed, complete ending.

beats.name: the divide
beats.purpose: establish the two worlds and the barrier between them

beats.name: the forbidden spark
beats.purpose: bring the lovers together across the barrier

beats.name: the hidden truth
beats.purpose: plant the secret of parentage or identity that will resolve everything

beats.name: rising passion
beats.purpose: let the relationship become undeniable and public

beats.name: family opposition
beats.purpose: mobilize the older generation against it

beats.name: the schemer acts
beats.purpose: have the antagonist manufacture the misunderstanding that separates them

beats.name: separation and suffering
beats.purpose: spend a long stretch on the cost of being apart

beats.name: the revelation
beats.purpose: disclose the secret that dissolves the class barrier

beats.name: the schemer exposed
beats.purpose: unmask and punish the antagonist publicly

beats.name: reunion
beats.purpose: restore the lovers with every obstacle answered

beats.name: the wedding
beats.purpose: close the story completely; nothing is left running

episodic_and_frame.register: Latin American serial drama and its international descendants; the closed ending distinguishes it from the open soap opera
episodic_and_frame.caution: The form runs on reversals at a fixed cadence; an episode without one breaks the contract, but reversals that cost nothing produce the genre's reputation for weightlessness.

episodic_and_frame.name: time-loop iteration
episodic_and_frame.definition: The repeated-day structure: a protagonist relives an interval, learns the rules through iterations, exhausts hedonism and despair, and escapes by a change of character rather than of tactics.

beats.name: the first pass
beats.purpose: play the interval straight so the audience learns it

beats.name: the reset
beats.purpose: return to the start and let the horror of it register

beats.name: testing the rules
beats.purpose: establish what carries over and what does not

beats.name: exploitation
beats.purpose: use perfect information for pleasure and advantage

beats.name: the limit of exploitation
beats.purpose: show that nothing gained inside the loop persists

beats.name: despair
beats.purpose: run the iterations of futility, including self-destruction

beats.name: the other person
beats.purpose: make someone else's outcome the thing worth iterating for

beats.name: mastery
beats.purpose: compress many attempts into visible, earned competence

beats.name: the unsolvable element
beats.purpose: confront the one thing skill cannot fix

beats.name: the change that breaks the loop
beats.purpose: escape by becoming different, not by acting differently

beats.name: the day after
beats.purpose: let time move and show what the iterations cost

episodic_and_frame.register: science fiction, comedy, and literary fiction about habit and change
episodic_and_frame.caution: Repetition is the form's material and its danger; each iteration shown must advance knowledge, character, or the audience's understanding of the rules.

episodic_and_frame.name: framed retrospective
episodic_and_frame.definition: The in-medias-res frame: open at a crisis, cut to the origin, run the past forward until it catches the present, then continue past the opening image to the real ending.

beats.name: open at the crisis
beats.purpose: start at the story's most charged moment with nothing explained

beats.name: the question hangs
beats.purpose: freeze or pause on the question the flashback will answer

beats.name: back to the beginning
beats.purpose: establish the ordinary world the opening made strange

beats.name: the past escalates
beats.purpose: run the causal chain that leads toward the opening image

beats.name: the decision that made it inevitable
beats.purpose: reach the choice the audience has been waiting to understand

beats.name: the timelines converge
beats.purpose: arrive back at the opening, now legible

beats.name: past the opening
beats.purpose: continue the crisis forward into what the frame withheld

beats.name: escalation in the present
beats.purpose: raise the stakes above what the opening implied

beats.name: climax
beats.purpose: resolve the situation the whole structure was engineered to charge

beats.name: the reframed close
beats.purpose: answer the opening image with what it turned out to mean

episodic_and_frame.aka: in medias res frame, flashback structure
episodic_and_frame.register: thriller, crime, literary fiction, and film; extremely common as a chapter-one device
episodic_and_frame.caution: The frame borrows tension against the flashback; if the past section is not itself dramatic, the audience spends it waiting rather than watching.

episodic_and_frame.name: serial installment cliffhanger
episodic_and_frame.definition: The installment structure: each unit opens on a hook, delivers its own complete movement, and closes on an unresolved reversal that makes the next unit necessary.

beats.name: the hook
beats.purpose: open in motion; the reader has decided by the second paragraph

beats.name: recap by implication
beats.purpose: restate what is at stake without summarizing the last installment

beats.name: installment goal
beats.purpose: set an objective the unit can genuinely settle

beats.name: complication
beats.purpose: oppose the goal with something specific to this unit

beats.name: the local turn
beats.purpose: deliver a reversal that pays this installment on its own

beats.name: consequence
beats.purpose: let the turn cost something that carries forward

beats.name: the serial thread
beats.purpose: advance the long arc by one visible increment

beats.name: apparent resolution
beats.purpose: settle the local question so the unit feels complete

beats.name: the reversal
beats.purpose: undercut the resolution in the last beat

beats.name: the cliff
beats.purpose: end on the unanswered question, not on the explanation

episodic_and_frame.register: serialized fiction, web serials, comics, and chapter-level plotting in commercial novels
episodic_and_frame.caution: A cliffhanger that resolves trivially at the next opening teaches readers not to worry; the reversal has to still be true on the next page.
